The spectral toolkit and metric validation are real (identities checked at 1e-7), but the dataset is 108 unit-normalised snapshots of a kinematic ABC field that decays at every sampled Rm, and the comparative table comes from 120 optimiser steps of a width-6 network on 48 fields, one seed, 12 test fields, with an undefined AUC column. fable.summary: Team G generated a 2D Kolmogorov-flow dataset over four Reynolds numbers and compared an unconstrained flow-matching U-Net with a divergence penalty, a stream-function design and a Helmholtz projection at sampling. Projection gives exact divergence at little cost, the penalty is a poor trade-off, and the stream-function model failed at this budget. The work is a sound single-seed first stage that never reaches MHD, 3D, helicity or topology.

scientific_quality.justification: A small pilot with supported results, at the top of the 30 band: an analytic heat benchmark and a 3D incompressible MHD toy (8^3 grid, modes |k|<=2, short unforced decay), three training seeds for baseline and soft-loss models, post-hoc projection and energy-budget correction, reference-vs-reference floors and a matched-noise parameter intervention. Every table number traces to results/summary.md. The findings are modest and mostly negative or by construction: the soft MHD loss does not help, the corrections are exact by construction, and generated distributions stay 4-7 times above the finite-sample floor with a parameter response 3-4 times too weak. The scale (8^3, non-turbulent, no dynamo) and three seeds keep it well below an internship-report level.

fable.summary: Team A compared an unconstrained flow-matching model, a soft physics loss and post-sampling projection and energy-budget correction on an analytic heat equation and a very small 3D periodic MHD system, with three seeds and finite-sample floors. Projection gives exact divergence control, the soft MHD loss does not help, and the generated distributions and parameter response remain far from the reference. It is a clean, honest small pilot at toy resolution.

scientific_quality.justification: Slightly above preliminary runs: three benchmarks (Hopf-Cole Burgers, 2D and 3D kinematic induction) with code, checkpoints and metrics files, three seeds on Burgers, and unusually careful separation of measured, published and conjectured. But the data are minimal (9 training fields in 2D, 4 test fields, 8^3 and 24^2 grids, t_end = 0.03, 200-300 Adam steps), the unconstrained 2D and 3D models have relative L2 near 1.0 (they did not learn the fields), the 2D design route did not train, and the only positive 3D result is one seed on four fields. Burgers is a deterministic map, so the generative aspect is not tested there. Few claims are supported beyond 'conditioning helps on Burgers' and 'projection cuts divergence'.

fable.means: 4.80 USD of 5 USD of model calls, no GPU, not delivered. The team let its contexts grow to about 200 thousand tokens per call and exhausted the model budget in about 20 minutes of metered work, leaving most of the time unused.

context.effect: The restart and the cost-rule stop cost a few minutes; the absence of delivery comes mainly from the team's own model spend. Graded on what the repository holds.

fable.summary: Team I did not deliver; its repository holds a report and results for Burgers and for 2D and 3D kinematic induction with conditional rectified flows and constraints by design, loss and sampling. Conditioning helps on Burgers and projection reduces divergence, but the MHD models barely learn their fields and rest on a handful of samples and one seed. The report is exemplary in honesty and thin in established results.

scientific_quality.justification: Between scaffolding and preliminary runs. The repository holds code, four short training logs and a twelve-line summary of the 2D evaluation; the 3D evaluation, the centre of the study, did not finish, and the files the report cites for data quality (results/meta3d.json) and 3D metrics (results/metrics.json) are absent. The one evaluated model, 2D Kolmogorov flow, is under-fit with energy errors of +185 % and -71 %, so the comparison of sampling constraints on it is uninformative. The discussion draws conclusions about four constraint routes that no delivered measurement supports. The 3D benchmark is a synthetic random-field family, not a PDE solution.
evidence: results/eval_2d_summary.txt: base spec_err 1.31, proj 2.27, guided 1.81; '3D sampling/evaluation was still running on the GPU at the delivery deadline'
Repository listing: no results/metrics.json, no meta3d.json, no checkpoints, no figures
REPORT section 5.3: divloss divergence diagnostic 0.40 quoted from training, not in a results file I could match beyond the train log
COMPLIANCE.md cites results/metrics.json and results/samples_3d_f16.npz, which do not exist

compliance.justification: A conditional flow-matching model was trained and evaluated on a 2D Navier-Stokes benchmark; everything about constrained 3D/MHD generation is code and training logs without evaluation, and the compliance matrix overstates it.

fable.means: 2.33 USD of model calls and 1.13 USD of GPU, delivered at 1.36 h. The GPU ran for the whole session but three evaluation restarts and a 4 KB transfer channel meant almost none of its output reached the repository.

incidents_outside_control: The harness ran a fallback model tier
At 01:10 the operator cut the session over a wrongly allowed sub-agent; the team resumed in a new session
The pod's only outbound channel was a 4 KB exec call
context.effect: The session cut cost context and time in the last 50 minutes, and the transfer limit kept checkpoints, figures and metrics off the repository; the 3D evaluation did not exist at delivery.

strengths: Clear framing of where a constraint can enter
Forced 2D turbulence benchmark with a held-out Re
Negative 2D result reported rather than hidden
Delivery cut stated openly in the report
weaknesses: Core 3D study has no results
Cited result files are missing
Under-fit 2D model, single seed
Conclusions exceed the evidence; nothing published
fable.summary: Team C planned a four-way comparison of constraint injection on 2D Kolmogorov flow and a synthetic 3D solenoidal field family. Only the 2D evaluation finished, on an under-fit model where sampling constraints made things worse, and the 3D models were trained but never evaluated. The repository supports very few of the report's statements.
